The mini‐modules further exhibit stable operation, maintaining over 85% of initial performance after 800 h (ISOS‐L1) and 89.7% after 300 thermal cycles between ‐40°C to 85°C. The preservation of key photovoltaic parameters suggests that the absorber bandgap remains intact at the module scale. To assess tandem relevance, a 4 cm
                    2
                    WBG mini‐module was used as the optical filter on a silicon heterojunction cell in a four‐terminal configuration, yielding a combined power output of 27.8%.

title: Reaction‐Programmed Dual‐State Molecular Engineering Decouples Mechanical Reinforcement and Ion Transport for Durable Flexible Zinc Devices
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Flexible aqueous zinc‐ion batteries demand hydrogel electrolytes that simultaneously reconcile mechanical durability, fast ion transport, and stable electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Yet abundant polar groups in conventional polyacrylamide hydrogels strongly coordinate Zn
                    2+
                    , creating an intrinsic trade‐off between network reinforcement and ionic mobility. Here, we report a reaction‐programmed bound‐free dual‐state molecular engineering strategy using acetylurea to orchestrate the polymer network, Zn
                    2+
                    coordination, and aqueous microenvironment. Initially, acetylurea acts as a molecular patch, reacting with polyacrylamide through Schiff‐base chemistry to form a dynamic imine‐crosslinked network that reinforces interchain coupling while shielding excessive Zn
                    2+
                    trapping. The optimized hydrogel thus sustains 6100% fracture strain while retaining near‐liquid ionic conductivity (19.1 mS cm
                    −1
                    ). After reactive sites approach saturation, free acetylurea reconstructs the Zn
                    2+
                    solvation sheath and hydrogen‐bond network, lowers water activity, accelerates desolvation, and homogenizes interfacial Zn
                    2+
                    flux. This cooperative regulation suppresses dendrites and parasitic reactions, enabling highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle for over 10 000 h, while Zn||MnO
                    2
                    and Zn||C devices sustain 4000 and 10 000 cycles, respectively, with integrated sensing/electrochemical functions retained after ∼100 000 bending cycles. This molecular program decouples mechanical reinforcement from ion transport across fundamentally distinct intercalation and capacitive charge‐storage mechanisms, establishing a general design principle for durable, deformable aqueous electrochemical systems.

title: Sleep pressure is increased by protein fragments and decreased by processive proteolysis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Sleep is universal among animals, yet the molecular-level causes and functions of sleep are incompletely understood. The fragment generation hypothesis (FGH) posits that sleep, at least in part, is an adaptive response to protein fragments, many of them protein-sized, that accumulate during wakefulness owing to cleavages by proteases, including caspases and Ca
                    2+
                    -activated calpains. According to the FGH, these fragments are a source of homeostatic sleep pressure that increases during wakefulness, and one function of sleep is to decrease protein fragment levels through their slower production and faster degradation during sleep. Predictions of the FGH have not previously been tested. Using zebrafish, we show that pharmacological inhibition of caspases decreases sleep, in agreement with the prediction of the FGH that a slower production of protein fragments would decrease sleep pressure. Pharmacological inhibition of the proteasome is shown to have the opposite effect, an increased sleep, in agreement with another prediction of the FGH, that sleep pressure would increase if fragments are protected from their proteasome-mediated degradation. Consistent with this prediction, a caspase-generated subunit of the activated caspase-3 is strongly upregulated by a sleep-increasing inhibition of the proteasome. The increase of sleep by proteasome inhibitors was found to be reduced by inhibition of calpains, suggesting that calpain-generated, proteasome-degradable protein fragments contribute to sleep pressure. Pharmacological inhibition of calpains also causes a decrease in rebound sleep after sleep deprivation, as predicted by the FGH. Together, these results suggest that the FGH may provide a molecular-level explanation of a cause and function of sleep.

title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS
                    2
                    achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl
                    −
                    induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens’ dispersal
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of
                    Homo sapiens
                    , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and
                    H. sapiens
                    lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of
                    H. sapiens
                    remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and
                    H. sapiens
                    dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from
                    Drosophila
                    embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

title: Steering nanometric reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycle for PFAS mineralization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:

Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the
                    a
                    -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that
                    a
                    -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish
                    sst6
                    (
                    sst6.2
                    ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited
                    sst6
                    mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including
                    pou5f1
                    ,
                    nanog
                    , and
                    sox2
                    , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. Here, we show, via a dynamic seismic cycle model incorporating spontaneous fault zone evolution through damage and healing, that both small and large earthquakes on a single fault emerge naturally from the interplay of fault slip and fault zone inelastic deformation. Our simulations reproduce key observations: frequency-magnitude distribution consistent with the Gutenberg-Richter law, magnitude-invariant static stress drop, and the dual-regime scaling of fracture energy density with earthquake magnitude. The results underscore the coevolution of earthquakes and fault zone damage as a fundamental mechanism governing earthquake behavior in nature. Fault zone deformation causing multiscale seismicity indicates that continuous monitoring of fault zone material properties may reveal fault stress states and earthquake potential.

title: ACSS2 modulates endothelial glycolysis in angiogenesis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Endothelial cells (ECs) sustain high glycolytic flux and display remarkable metabolic plasticity. Although molecular pathways regulating endothelial glycolysis are well characterized, metabolic mechanisms underlying hypoxia-induced glycolytic activation during angiogenesis remain poorly understood. Here, we show that acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2) serves as a critical metabolic modulator, coupling acetate utilization with glycolytic flux to control EC function and angiogenesis. The high level of ACSS2-mediated acetate-to-acetyl-CoA conversion in angiogenic front ECs sustains acetyl-CoA levels, which are essential for EC proliferation and retinal vascularization. Conversely, endothelial-specific
                    Acss2
                    deletion disrupts pathological angiogenesis and normalizes tumor vasculature. Mechanistically, ACSS2 maintains hypoxia-inducible factor 1α transcriptional activity and stabilizes glucose transporter 1, thereby preserving glycolysis. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 knockdown rescues metabolic and functional defects in ACSS2-deficient ECs, revealing the vital role of acetyl-CoA homeostasis in modulating hypoxic endothelial metabolism. Taken together, these data establish ACSS2 as a pivotal regulator of vascular development and suggest that targeting acetate metabolism may be an effective way to modulate pathological angiogenesis.

title: An ensemble of functionally distinct factors enables spatial quality control during proteasome base assembly
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The proteasome is an essential mediator of the ubiquitin–proteasome system and a complex molecular machine. Hallmarks of de novo proteasome assembly include dedicated chaperones and many subunits, culminating into major assembly intermediates such as the base. Emerging evidence suggests that proteasome assembly is subject to extensive quality control (QC). To understand mechanisms of QC, we examined a crucial assembly checkpoint during base assembly. Our findings reveal sequential mechanisms of QC, in which a checkpoint complex is first assembled, then sequestered into the nucleus, away from ongoing proteasome assembly in the cytoplasm. Assembly of this checkpoint complex depends on noncanonical ubiquitination of the Nas2 chaperone. The Nas2 ubiquitin chain functions as a scaffold by binding the Rpn13 ubiquitin receptor, which is distantly positioned within the same complex. Rpn13 also positions the ubiquitin chain to its neighboring Hul5 ubiquitin ligase, for continual chain elongation to further stabilize this complex. Ubiquitin-mediated assembly enables spatial sequestration of this checkpoint complex through its intrinsic nuclear localization signal (NLS). This NLS on Rpt4 specifically targets this checkpoint complex into the nucleus, emphasizing the importance of spatial compartmentalization. Our findings reveal that proteasome assembly integrates multiple functionally distinct components as QC factors (1 assembly chaperone, 2 ubiquitin regulators, and 1 NLS) to distinguish correct vs. incorrect assembly events en route to a proteasome holoenzyme. These components are not simply passengers in assembly intermediates with their activities reserved for mature proteasomes, but their fundamental functions in cellular proteolysis may begin by first ensuring the accuracy of proteasome assembly.

title: Basal radial glia abundance and morphotype diversity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus imply their evolutionarily ancient origin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Basal radial glia (bRG) are neural progenitor cells (NPCs) essential for primate neocortical expansion, but their presence in other brain regions and across species remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the developing mouse dentate gyrus (DG), unlike the neocortex, harbors abundant NPCs that transcriptionally and morphologically resemble human neocortical bRG. This striking abundance is conserved across other Boreoeutherian species, including mice, marmosets, ferrets, and pigs. Comparative transcriptomics uncovered a shared morphoregulatory gene signature between bRG in mouse DG and human neocortex. Immunohistochemical analysis showed diversity in DG bRG morphotypes across species. Remarkably, compared to the neocortex, DG bRG consistently exhibit greater morphotype diversity. Ancestral state reconstruction suggests that this diversity was already present in the common ancestor of Boreoeutherians. Together, our findings position the DG as a conserved, evolutionarily ancient niche for bRG, revealing that region- and species-specific adaptations of NPCs extend beyond the neocortex.

title: ATAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation drives pancreatic tumorigenesis through DNMT1-mediated regulation of NDRG4
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Microtubule (MT) acetylation is frequently elevated in cancer and associated with poor prognosis. Alpha-tubulin acetyltransferase 1 (ATAT1), the principal enzyme responsible for this modification, has therefore emerged as a potential therapeutic target. However, which cancer types depend on ATAT1 activity and are selectively vulnerable to its inhibition remains unclear. Here, using a phospho-specific marker of ATAT1 activity, we identify pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) as an ATAT1-dependent malignancy. ATAT1 activity is elevated in human PDAC and genetically engineered mouse models, emerging during pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia and persisting in a substantial subset of tumors. Genetic inactivation or pharmacologic inhibition of ATAT1 suppresses PDAC cell growth, reduces orthotopic tumor burden, and markedly inhibits tumor initiation in KPC mice without overt toxicity. Mechanistically, ATAT1-dependent MT acetylation sustains Akt signaling, resulting in inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β and stabilization of the DNA methyltransferase DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1). Elevated DNMT1 promotes repression of tumor suppressor genes, including NDRG4, whereas inhibition of ATAT1 or DNMT1 restores NDRG4 expression and impairs tumor growth. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized ATAT1-Akt-GSK3β-DNMT1 signaling axis linking cytoskeletal acetylation to NDRG4 repression and reveal ATAT1 as a therapeutic vulnerability during the early stages of pancreatic tumorigenesis.

title: Biological stochasticity increases the evolutionary limit of lifespan
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The mutation accumulation theory attributes aging to the decline in selection strength with age. While classical models assume fixed ages of mutation expression, empirical evidence reveals significant interindividual variation in the timing of mutation expression. Here, we develop mathematical models incorporating this stochasticity. By tracking the fate of lethal mutations, we characterize the boundary of the “selection shadow” where genetic drift overcomes purging selection against such mutations—a fundamental evolutionary limit, termed the lifespan drift barrier, setting a theoretical benchmark for the pace of aging. Our results show that for both stochastic age- and state-dependent mutations, variation in the age of mutation expression generally pushes back this lifespan drift barrier. This outcome is a universal consequence of the inherent convexity of the selection gradient under extrinsic mortality: early expression in a subset of individuals intensifies purging selection, thereby raising the drift barrier. In addition, we demonstrate that while this variance shifts this evolutionary threshold (determining the pace of aging), it leaves the mortality trajectory at mutation–selection balance (the shape of aging) fundamentally unaltered. These findings thus help explain how the pace and shape of aging can become uncoupled.

title: Curvature-guided chiral collective organization of myoblast tissues
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Surface curvature is a fundamental geometric cue in tissue morphogenesis, yet its role in guiding collective cell organization has remained elusive. Here, we show that curvature acts as a geometric control parameter that shapes supracellular alignment and chirality while modulating myogenic differentiation in myoblast tissues. Cells cultured on curved substrates self-organize into robust helical assemblies whose handedness is set, and can be reversed, by the sign of curvature: convex fibers produce right-handed helices, whereas concave channels invert the chirality. We identify a clockwise bias in single-cell motion associated with the helical actin cytoskeleton. A minimal continuum theory coupling an effective chiral drive to curvature quantitatively captures the emergence and reversal of tissue-scale chiral alignment. On substrates with spatially varying curvature, local curvature gradients organize patterned multicellular architectures while preserving a global handedness. Curvature is also associated with myogenic state, with higher curvature linked to reduced or delayed differentiation. Together, these findings reveal how complex geometries shape the alignment, symmetry, and cellular state of living tissues.

title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

title: Four phases and temporal threshold of population calcium response during locomotion in cortical astrocytes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Calcium activity is a major form of astrocyte excitability. Astrocytic calcium events arise spontaneously and in response to behavior, but how unitary events shape population-level activity remains unclear. Using two-photon imaging in the primary somatosensory cortex of awake mice running on a freely rotating disk, we analyzed calcium dynamics during quiescence and locomotion. During quiescence, population fluctuations were driven mainly by the co-occurrence of new events rather than by their enlargement. During locomotion, responses progressed through four phases: emergence of new events, their merging into a superevent, fragmentation, and an afterburst. These responses combined the progressive recruitment of active regions with amplification of a reproducible spatial calcium pattern. New events emerged within the first seconds after locomotion onset, indicating a rapid astrocytic response. A full population response required about 5 s of locomotion: Shorter episodes failed to develop the superevent and produced markedly smaller responses. In suprathreshold episodes, the superevent displayed a reproducible ΔF/F pattern. Hotspots within this pattern had shorter latencies and were also more active during quiescence. A dynamic mode decomposition with control model driven by synthetic or real locomotion inputs reproduced the response phases, temporal threshold, and superevent pattern. These findings show that locomotion-evoked astrocytic calcium activity is an ordered, threshold-dependent population process with reproducible spatiotemporal structure that can be approximated by a low-dimensional dynamical system.

title: Neuronal IL-34 programs microglial activity via the TGF-β–MEF2C axis to constrain neuroinflammation following brain ischemia
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Brain ischemia induces robust neuroinflammation driven by microglial activation, yet whether ischemic neurons actively reprogram microglial phenotypes to limit inflammation remains elusive. Here, we identify neuronal interleukin-34 (IL-34) as a critical immunomodulatory signal that maintains microglial homeostasis after cerebral ischemia. We demonstrate that ischemic injury augments IL-34-CSF1R signaling between neurons and microglia. Neuron-specific overexpression of
                    Il34
                    (Syn1-
                    Il34
                    tg
                    mice) attenuated infarct volume and neurodeficits after middle cerebral artery occlusion, whereas neuronal
                    Il34
                    knockdown exacerbated brain injury. Microglial depletion abolished IL-34-mediated neuroprotection, suggesting microglia as essential effectors. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that neuronal IL-34 preserved homeostatic microglial signatures (
                    P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Tgfbr1
                    ), while suppressing inflammatory activities (
                    Il1b, Tnf, Cxcl2
                    ) through upregulation of the transcription factor MEF2C. Mechanistically, IL-34 activated TGF-β signaling in microglia and inhibition of TGF-β signaling abolished the protective effects of IL-34, whereas microglia-specific
                    Mef2c
                    overexpression rescued neuroprotection despite TGF-β blockade. Thus, ischemic neurons deploy IL-34 to orchestrate the immunoregulatory activity of microglia via the TGF-β–MEF2C axis, representing a previously unrecognized endogenous mechanism counteracting neuroinflammation. Our study reveals neuronal IL-34 as a potential therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

title: Local influenza forecasts outperform state-level forecasts in the United States
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Accurate outbreak forecasts are critical for timely and effective public health response. In the United States, however, most forecasts are produced at the state level, which can mask substantial substate heterogeneity and limit their utility for local planning. We generated and evaluated forecasts of the percentage of Emergency Department visits attributable to influenza across 173 large metropolitan Health Service Areas (HSAs) using a gradient boosting quantile regression model and compared their accuracy to forecasts derived from state-level data alone. At a 1-wk, 2-wk, and 3-wk horizon, local forecasts outperformed state-based forecasts in 98.8%, 90.8%, and 78.6% of HSAs, respectively, achieving mean weighted interval scores that were on average a 39.2% lower (95% range: 5.9 to 76.7%), 19.6% lower (−6.3 to 59.5%), and 11.4% lower (−11.7 to 44.9%), respectively. The performance advantage of local forecasting was strongest in HSAs representing a smaller share of their state’s population and increased with the proportion of the HSA population living in urban areas and the number of metropolitan areas within a state. These results, based on an analysis of HSAs with populations greater than 250,000, demonstrate that fine-scale modeling can substantially improve forecast accuracy and highlight the potential value of local forecasts for outbreak preparedness and response.

title: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal fungal taxa, limiting our capacity to forecast future shifts in community composition and function. Here, we use 115,924 DNA sequence-derived observations to map the distribution of 651 common mycorrhizal fungal taxa and forecast future changes to their range sizes. We demonstrate that climate, plant cover, and soil factors, particularly mean annual temperature, net primary productivity, and soil organic carbon, exert major control over mycorrhizal fungal distributions. Based on these drivers, the ecological niches of mycorrhizal fungi consistently differ between arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal functional guilds. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal taxa generally occupy a wider niche breadth than ectomycorrhizal fungi, occurring across larger ranges of climate, soil, plant cover, topography, and disturbance conditions. Our models also predict widespread decreases in the suitable range size of mycorrhizal fungal taxa under projected future global climates, with average ranges decreasing by 13.8% or ~2.2 million km
                    2
                    under high emissions scenarios (ssp5-8.5). This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of common mycorrhizal fungi and their associated environmental niche, we establish a critical baseline for widely suspected declines in global fungal biodiversity.

title: Competing capillary pathways govern buckling in drying porous microcapsules
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Capillary forces are fundamental in nature, lifting water in plants and supporting insects on ponds. Here, we show that capillary force can also buckle porous microcapsules as they dry. As water evaporates through the polymeric shell, an asymmetric air–polymer–water interface emerges and expands, where concave menisci at interfacial nanopores generate capillary (Laplace) pressure that deforms the shell. Optical imaging and accompanying phase-field modeling show that buckling initiates once the capillary pressure spreads over a critical surface area, then proceeds quasi-statically: Dimples nucleate, deepen, and ultimately evolve into a nested, double-shelled morphology, with each step rate-limited by water drainage through the porous shell. If the air–water front penetrates the microcapsule interior before buckling starts, the capillary loading area collapses and buckling is prevented. Drying therefore follows two competing capillary pathways: One drives buckling by sustaining distributed capillary loading on the shell, whereas the other suppresses buckling through early interior air invasion. Inspired by this insight, we preintroduce an internal air bubble into each microcapsule to act as a capillary sink and bias drying toward the air-invasion pathway. Our findings provide a mechanics-based blueprint guiding the design of robust, dry-stable microcapsules for pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and beyond.

title: Localized end-on heating for hot spot ignition in precompressed isochoric plasmas
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In fast ignition inertial confinement fusion, a “heating cone” is employed to shorten the transport distance of the relativistic electron beam (REB) to the high-density plasma core, thereby mitigating energy losses at the plasma edge. However, its insertion depth and survival time are constrained by the sustained pressure from the large-scale plasma edge during the implosion process. Our whole-process simulations demonstrated that, in the double-cone ignition scheme, the head-on collision of two deuterium-tritium plasma jets not only forms a high-density plateau with a small-scale edge, but also substantially reduces the interaction time between the heating cone and the colliding plasma to approximately
                    
                      
                        
                          0.1
                          
                          ns
                        
                      
                    
                    . This shortened interaction time enables the heating cone to remain intact after the peak compression, even when placed directly at the small-scale edge of the colliding plasma. The small-scale edge is compatible with the range of the soft-spectrum REB generated by the heating lasers. Such a REB efficiently heats a localized end-on hot spot adjacent to the high-density plateau, guided by a kT-level magnetic field amplified from a seed field during the collision process. Ignited by the localized hot spot, the high-density plateau can undergo sufficient burning and achieve a fusion energy gain of 6.8 using

title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Language model teams as distributed systems
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are growing increasingly powerful. Yet, fundamental constraints on the reasoning, memory, and performance of individual models has sparked recent interest in scaling abilities using LLM teams. With growing deployment of LLM teams at scale, there is a need for principled guidelines for when teams help, how many agents to use, and how structure impacts performance. Rather than building these teams through trial-and-error, we propose using distributed systems as a formal foundation for designing and evaluating LLM teams. Under this formal framework, we derive predictions about how task structure and team architecture should shape performance. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: LLM team scaling follows classical distributed computing laws based on the structure of a task, and centralized and decentralized architectures exhibit the asymmetric vulnerabilities predicted by distributed systems theory. These results establish distributed computing as a generative framework that yields testable, quantitative predictions about LLM team behavior and informs the construction of more efficient and capable teams.

title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: Paul R. Ehrlich: Visionary pioneer and public scientist for nature and humanity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Paul R. Ehrlich is legendary for his scientific insight and impact—and even more so for bringing science to the public through writing, speaking, and, most famously, twenty-some appearances on the Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson. He was quick-witted—he would readily add quick-tempered, with chagrin—and could bring down a house. Paul cherished deep friendships and nature. He loved collaborating with his wife of 71 years, Anne H. Ehrlich, and with innumerable students and colleagues all over the world. He made transformative contributions of astonishing range, including in ecology and evolution, biodiversity and conservation, human population and overconsumption, and the integration of ecology and economics. He was deeply committed to racial and social justice, reflected in his actions and writing.

title: A periplasmic regulator establishes adaptive impermeability to control carbapenem entry
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Outer-membrane permeability is a major determinant of antibiotic susceptibility in Gram-negative bacteria and is generally thought to be controlled through transcriptional regulation of porin expression. Here we identify the small periplasmic protein PtrA as a regulator of OprD-dependent carbapenem permeability in
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    . PtrA promotes imipenem resistance without altering OprD abundance, associates with OprD-containing membrane complexes and reduces intracellular imipenem entry. Using zinc and copper as complementary physiological signals, we show that PtrA-mediated permeability control is mechanistically distinct from CzcRS-dependent repression of
                    oprD
                    and precedes transcriptional porin depletion. These findings define a two-phase mechanism in which rapid periplasmic regulation provides an immediate adaptive response before transcriptional remodeling of the outer membrane. Our work identifies adaptive impermeability as a previously unrecognized mechanism linking environmental sensing to dynamic control of bacterial outer-membrane permeability.

title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr
                    2+
                    –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3
                    +
                    microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1
                    +
                    dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

title: CD49f identifies stem-like memory T cells with enhanced therapeutic potency
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The efficacy of adoptive cell therapies depends on the presence of T cells with durable self-renewal, proliferative capacity, and differentiation potential, yet heterogeneity within starting cell populations remains a major barrier to consistent clinical outcomes. Here, we identify CD49f as a marker of a unique subset of human memory T cells with stem-like characteristics. CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory CD8
                    +
                    and CD4
                    +
                    T cells exhibited transcriptional and phenotypic features associated with T cell stemness, including elevated LEF1, TCF1, CCR7, CD27, and CD28, while CD49f
                    Lo
                    cells exhibited effector-like transcriptional programs. Clinical evaluation of solid-organ transplant recipients treated with virus-specific T cells for cytomegalovirus complications demonstrated that autologous T cell therapies manufactured from CD49f
                    Hi
                    -enriched T cells were associated with superior immune reconstitution and greater in vivo expansion of CMV-specific T cells. Functional assays further revealed that CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory T cells possessed enhanced proliferative capacity and transcriptional plasticity following activation. Consistent with these findings, CD19 CAR T cells engineered from CD49f
                    Hi
                    memory T cells demonstrated improved persistence and conferred superior survival in a preclinical lymphoma model. Together, these findings establish CD49f as a marker of a stem-like memory T cell subset with enhanced therapeutic potential and identify CD49f
                    Hi
                    enrichment as a practical strategy to improve the consistency, durability, and clinical efficacy of both virus-specific and CAR T cell therapies.
